summit.title: Three stars, one coast
summit.story: The Algarve's top tables were for decades all resort houses west of Faro. Vila Joya, on the cliff at Praia da Galé in Albufeira, has held two stars under Dieter Koschina since 1999, after a first in 1995. Ocean, inside Vila Vita Parc at Porches, cooks a different Discovery-route menu each year under Hans Neuner, and its restaurant manager took MICHELIN's Best Service Award in 2025. In March 2026 Faro got its first star: Alameda, where Rui Sequeira, once Ocean's sous-chef, ties a tasting menu to Algarve legends. Both two-star houses have taken winter breaks, Ocean reopening only in March in 2025; Alameda reports no seasonal closure.
summit.where: Alameda, Faro Centro; Vila Joya, Albufeira; Ocean, Porches

stories.title: An island and a street
stories.story: Two of Faro's tables with a past sit at opposite ends of a boat ride. Estaminé is the only building on Ilha da Barreta, the sand island across the Ria Formosa that the boats call Ilha Deserta; it burned in March 2021 and Animaris, which runs the boats, rebuilt it to work on solar power and make its own water. Inside the walls, on Rua do Castelo, Leonel Pereira left the starred kitchen of São Gabriel in 2020 to open CHECKin, a smaller room that won a Bib Gourmand in 2021 and moved into its present rooms in 2022. One is lunch only and depends on the boat; the other is dinner, Monday to Saturday.
stories.where: Estaminé, Ilha Deserta; CHECKin by Leonel Pereira, Cidade Velha

tascas.title: Copper pots and small rooms
tascas.story: Faro's tascas cook the Ria Formosa in a short, fixed vocabulary: the cataplana steamed shut in its copper pot, wet razor-clam rice, clams with garlic and coriander, fish off the grill. Tasca do Ricky on Rua do Forno keeps nine tables of four at most and builds its name on the cataplana the owner recommends. A Venda on Rua do Compromisso does petiscos from scratch in a room of old furniture and odd plates, with a large vegetarian list. Adega Nova, near the station, is the big room where families celebrate over picanha cooked on a hot stone. All three are small or plain enough that hours shift, and A Venda may close for winter, so call.
tascas.where: Tasca do Ricky, Faro Centro; A Venda, Faro Centro; Adega Nova, Faro Centro

street.title: Two markets and a bifana
street.story: The street food of this coast is bought where the fish comes in, and eaten before noon. Faro's own Mercado Municipal is the plain city market off the Largo Dr. Francisco Sá Carneiro, its present building nineteen years old in February 2026: fish and shellfish on one side, fruit and greens on the other. At its counter Snack Bar da Xica opens at seven and sells the bifana for cash. Ten minutes east by train, Olhão's two waterfront halls are the fishing port's own market and the one to show a chef. All three are morning places: by early afternoon the stalls are closing.
street.where: Mercado Municipal de Faro, Faro Centro; Mercado de Olhão, Olhão; Snack Bar da Xica, Mercado Municipal de Faro
